- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5.0), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 3–4x the recent 7-day average to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model underestimates; add 5–15% buffer to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model underperforms in low-sentiment periods with stable history; increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment is low and recent price range is narrow.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 10-day average is >2.5, forecast should not exceed 2.0 unless sentiment is strong.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 5–10% if sentiment is rising or recent price is trending up.
